# Export-ZbxAgentTemplate

## SYNOPSIS

Exports the host an agent session provisioned, with its interface and items.

## SYNTAX

### Pipeline (Default)

```
Export-ZbxAgentTemplate [-Session] <string> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] [-Unredacted] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Path

```
Export-ZbxAgentTemplate [-Session] <string> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -Path <string> [-NoClobber] [-Unredacted] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### LiteralPath

```
Export-ZbxAgentTemplate [-Session] <string> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -LiteralPath <string> [-NoClobber] [-Unredacted] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Export-ZbxAgentTemplate cmdlet exports, with configuration.export, the host Initialize-ZbxAgentHost provisioned for the agent session named in -Session: the host, its agent interface and its items, as a document Import-ZbxConfiguration reads back. -Format chooses JSON (the default), XML or YAML, and -Path writes the document to a file instead of the pipeline. Plaintext secrets are redacted unless -Unredacted is given.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Export the agent's host as JSON

```powershell
Export-ZbxAgentTemplate -Session 'web-agent' | ConvertFrom-Json | ForEach-Object { $_.zabbix_export.hosts.host }
```

The document's hosts section holds the host with its interface and items.

### Example 2: Save the export as YAML

```powershell
$path = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "web-agent-$PID.yaml"
Export-ZbxAgentTemplate -Session 'web-agent' -Format Yaml -Path $path
Get-Content $path -TotalCount 5
Remove-Item $path
```

-Path writes the file and nothing to the pipeline; -NoClobber keeps a file that exists.
